papers.title: Can Learning Deteriorate Control? Analyzing Computational Delays in Gaussian Process-Based Event-Triggered Online Learning
papers.abstract: When the dynamics of systems are unknown, supervised machine learning techniques are commonly employed to infer models from data. Gaussian process (GP) regression is a particularly popular learning method for this purpose due to the existence of prediction error bounds. Moreover, GP models can be efficiently updated online, such that event-triggered online learning strategies can be pursued to ensure specified tracking accuracies. However, existing trigger conditions must be able to be evaluated at arbitrary times, which cannot be achieved in practice due to non-negligible computation times. Therefore, we first derive a delay-aware tracking error bound, which reveals an accuracy-delay trade-off. Based on this result, we propose a novel event trigger for GP-based online learning with computational delays, which we show to offer advantages over offline trained GP models for sufficiently small computation times. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed event trigger for online learning in simulations.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于控制系统的在线学习延迟问题，与FEA代理建模或生物力学设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses computational delays in event-triggered control learning, not surrogate modeling, FEA validation, or biomechanical optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决在线学习中计算延迟导致的触发条件失效问题
summary_zh.method: 推导延迟感知跟踪误差界，提出新的事件触发机制
summary_zh.result: 延迟触发机制在计算时间足够小时优于离线训练模型
summary_zh.validation: 通过仿真验证延迟感知触发机制的有效性

summary_en.motivation: The paper addresses the problem that existing event-triggered learning conditions cannot be evaluated at arbitrary times due to computational delays.
summary_en.method: A delay-aware tracking error bound is derived, and a novel event trigger for Gaussian process-based online learning is proposed.
summary_en.result: The proposed trigger outperforms offline trained GP models when computation times are sufficiently small.
summary_en.validation: The effectiveness is demonstrated through simulations of unknown dynamical systems.

papers.title: Two is Better Than One: Digital Siblings to Improve Autonomous Driving Testing
papers.abstract: Simulation-based testing represents an important step to ensure the reliability of autonomous driving software. In practice, when companies rely on third-party general-purpose simulators, either for in-house or outsourced testing, the generalizability of testing results to real autonomous vehicles is at stake. In this paper, we enhance simulation-based testing by introducing the notion of digital siblings, a multi-simulator approach that tests a given autonomous vehicle on multiple general-purpose simulators built with different technologies, that operate collectively as an ensemble in the testing process.   We exemplify our approach on a case study focused on testing the lane-keeping component of an autonomous vehicle. We use two open-source simulators as digital siblings, and we empirically compare such a multi-simulator approach against a digital twin of a physical scaled autonomous vehicle on a large set of test cases. Our approach requires generating and running test cases for each individual simulator, in the form of sequences of road points. Then, test cases are migrated between simulators, using feature maps to characterize the exercised driving conditions. Finally, the joint predicted failure probability is computed, and a failure is reported only in cases of agreement among the siblings.   Our empirical evaluation shows that the ensemble failure predictor by the digital siblings is superior to each individual simulator at predicting the failures of the digital twin. We discuss the findings of our case study and detail how our approach can help researchers interested in automated testing of autonomous driving software.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文完全关于自动驾驶测试，与生物打印或AI在生物打印中的应用没有任何关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses autonomous driving simulation testing and has no connection to bioprinting, AI-driven bioprinting workflow, or any biomedical application.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高自动驾驶软件测试的可靠性。
summary_zh.method: 提出数字兄弟姐妹概念，利用多个不同技术的通用模拟器进行集成测试。
summary_zh.result: 数字兄弟姐妹的集成故障预测优于单个模拟器。
summary_zh.validation: 通过数字孪生物理车辆进行案例研究验证。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance the reliability of autonomous driving software through simulation-based testing.
summary_en.method: Introducing digital siblings, a multi-simulator ensemble approach that tests autonomous vehicles across different simulators and migrates test cases using feature maps.
summary_en.result: The ensemble failure predictor from digital siblings outperforms each individual simulator in predicting failures of a digital twin.
summary_en.validation: Empirical evaluation using a digital twin of a physical scaled autonomous vehicle.
